items.sentence: "Formosa" *is* commonly known as an unofficial name for Taiwan.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C

items.sentence: However, what many people don't know *is* that there is another Formosa located on the banks of the Paraguay River in Argentina.
items.pattern: Noun clause (S) + Vl + C + Noun clause (that...)

items.sentence: To explore this connection, we can *take* a closer look at these two namesakes to see how they are similar and how they differ.
items.pattern: Infinitival phrase + S + Vt (Phrasal verb) + O + Infinitival phrase + Noun clauses

items.sentence: Interestingly, it *appears* that both Formosas were unintentionally reached by European explorers in the sixteenth century.
items.pattern: It + Vi + Noun clause (that...)

items.sentence: It *is believed* that a crew of Portuguese sailors came across Taiwan and named it "Ilha Formosa," which means "beautiful island."
items.pattern: Passive reporting structure + Noun clause (that...) + Relative clause (which...)

items.sentence: Similarly, Formosa *was* the European name given to an area of land in South America by Spanish explorers around the same time.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C + Participial phrase (p.p.)

items.sentence: These explorers *decided* to settle there mainly because the area possessed an exceptional strategic location and economic advantages.
items.pattern: S + Vt + Infinitival O + Adverbial clause (because...)

items.sentence: Apart from their shared name and historical similarities, there *is* an interesting geographical fact that connects these two locations.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + There + Vi + S + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: Taiwan *is located* at 23° N and Argentina's Formosa at 23° S, which means both areas are roughly the same distance from the equator.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Prepositional phrase + Relative clause (which...)

items.sentence: What's more, each of them *sits* on the exact opposite side of the world from the other.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: If someone in northern Taiwan dug a hole straight down into the Earth, penetrated its core, and then continued digging to the surface on the other side, he or she would *end up* in Formosa, Argentina!
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (If...) with compound verbs + S + Vi (Phrasal verb) + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Since most of the globe is covered in ocean, it *is* remarkable to find that the two Formosas are exactly antipodal!
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (Since...) + It + Vl + C + Infinitival phrase + Noun clause (that...)

items.sentence: Despite these things that they have in common, the two Formosas *are*, in many ways, still worlds apart.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase with Relative clause (that...) + S + Vl + C

items.sentence: Their natural landscapes, for a start, *differ* considerably.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Adv

items.sentence: Two thirds of Taiwan's 36,000 square kilometers *are covered* with densely forested majestic mountains, some of which soar thousands of meters above sea level.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Prepositional phrase + Relative clause (of which...)

items.sentence: Furthermore, the island's mountains, valleys, rivers, and reefs *are* home to hundreds of unique species found only in Taiwan.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C + Participial phrase (p.p.)

items.sentence: By contrast, most of Argentina's Formosa, which is two times the size of Taiwan, *is* fairly flat and made up of trees, grassland, or marshland.
items.pattern: S + Relative clause (which...) + Vl + C (Compound complement)

items.sentence: Its eastern region *receives* more rain than its other parts and also *has* more forests and streams.
items.pattern: S + Vt (Compound verb) + O

items.sentence: There *is*, in addition, a stark contrast between their economies.
items.pattern: There + Vi + S + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Present-day Taiwan *is known* worldwide for its lively economy and its advanced information technology industry.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Moreover, the Asian island *is* famous for its natural beauty and friendly people and thus *attracts* visitors from far and wide.
items.pattern: S + Vi / Vt (Compound verb) + C / O

items.sentence: By contrast, Formosa *is* one of Argentina's least developed areas.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C

items.sentence: Its economy *relies* primarily on raising cattle and other agricultural activities such as growing cotton and fruit.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Prepositional phrase + Gerund phrase

items.sentence: The number of cattle in the area *exceeds* 1.5 million, which is more than three times the number of people living there!
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Relative clause (which...)

items.sentence: Whatever differences or similarities exist between the pair, each *has* a beauty that makes it special.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (Whatever...) + S + Vt + O + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: Both Argentina's Formosa, with its gorgeous green plains and lush forests, and Taiwan, with its bustling cities and mighty, mountainous landscapes, *are* sure to impress visitors.
items.pattern: Compound S + Vl + C + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: Perhaps the people of these two lands on opposite sides of the world could even *come* face to face one day as well and *get* to know each other a little better!
items.pattern: S + Vi / Vt (Compound verb) + C / Infinitival O

items.sentence: That would *make for* a beautiful friendship!
items.pattern: S + Vt (Phrasal verb) + O
